coupling: fdaa147 narrows the AI7 width and height to uint32_t before the product checks and returns 3 times that truncated product, still capped by maxAi7ThumbnailSize. On its own that is a tighter ceiling: the decoder it shipped with only uses the returned length to stop a growing buffer, so a truncated size cannot write past an allocation. 67b117d replaces that decoder with one preallocated to the helper's byte count, but bounds the fill by width*height*3 — the same expression makePnm asserts, and exactly the value the helper returned before the narrowing. For every thumbnail the un-narrowed helper accepts, that limit equals the allocation, so the rewrite stays in range. The out-of-bounds write appears only when both land together: the buffer is the truncated uint32 product while the loop runs to the full geometric size. Repairing either diff restores one side of that contract (size_t arithmetic rejects this input before decode, or the fill ceiling is the allocation again), so the fault is not visible in, or reachable from, either edit alone.
